implementation_notes: A function plus a queue is the whole endpoint: the worker awaits q.get(), calls the service and calls q.task_done() when the work (not the receipt) is finished - the standard-library example in the asyncio queue documentation is exactly this shape. That replaces the endpoint object and makes the acknowledgement boundary explicit, and a thread-backed queue.Queue with a worker thread is the same realization for blocking services. Celery-style task functions are the brokered version, where the worker pool provides competing consumers and the framework performs the acknowledgement; a hand-written adapter class is only needed when one endpoint dispatches by message type.
pitfalls: task_done() in a finally block acknowledges failures as processed; if the error must be retried, requeue the item before calling task_done().
A blocking call (requests, psycopg2, open()) inside the async worker stalls the whole event loop; use the thread-backed worker or run_in_executor.
A task created with create_task whose exception nobody awaits is reported as 'Task exception was never retrieved' and the message is lost; catch per message inside the loop.
